name: February
objective: Run Stronger in 30 2.0 (members-only, 1 Feb–2 Mar) as Q1's attendance engine; pair acquisition through Valentine's/Galentine's; finishers renew onto longer plans.
strategy:
Valentine's + Stronger in 30 2.0.

Commercial job: Run Stronger in 30 2.0 (members-only, 1 Feb–2 Mar) as Q1's attendance engine; pair acquisition through Valentine's/Galentine's; finishers renew onto longer plans.

Newcomer: Situationship → Relationship (“Stop situationship-ing your fitness. Two dates, then make it official.”). Kenkere's VDAY50! code (38 uses, ₹2.6L given away at 50%) bought February volume at a huge cost. This replaces 50% with a structured path: a booked second visit lifts conversion from 10.8% to 43.9%; the challenge gives a reason to keep coming.

Referral: Couples Therapy (Cheaper Than the Real Thing) (“Couples therapy, but cheaper and with better glutes.”). Referrals convert 41.2% at Kwality, 22.6% at Bandra, 28.3% at Kenkere and 76.1% at pop-ups, versus 3.8–5.7% for website leads. The 2026 BOGO codes (70 uses, ₹3.1L given) went mostly to existing clients; this only pays out when a new person buys.

Renewal: Proof of Work (“You did 30 in 30. Your renewal price should show it.”). Renewers average 6.4 visits in the first half of a membership vs 2.6–3.4 for lapsers; members using 75%+ of sessions renew 82–88% across studios. The best price only goes to proven attenders.

Lapsed: Galentine's Gone Ghost (“Your bestie's been ghosting the gym too? Come back together.”). Lapsed clients already know the product and bring friends who convert like referrals (22–76%). Pairing two hesitant people raises the odds both show up.
notes: Build: 55 new buyers × ₹11,150 first-60-day spend = ₹6.2L; 60 renewals × ₹23,384 = ₹14.1L; 27 winbacks = ₹3.1L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹2.3L. Offers carry ₹19.7L (77% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 51% CRM status, trial→member 26.9%) — not invented lifts.
